newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tanker chartering lack luster, undertone sta.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tanker chartering lack luster, undertone sta.

text.p: Dirty tanker chartering activity remained lacklustre with good tonnage avails in most regions fuelling strong competition for business, brokers said.
World scale rates in most regions were little changed but the market continued to carry a softer undertone as brokers competed actively to book the few fresh enquiries coming onto the market.
Mideast Gulf/Red Sea to eastern destinations continued to see sufficient business to hold rates for VLCCs steady with voyages to Japan holding around W56-7 and S.Korea around W52-55.
Rates to the West valued W50 for USG and W52.5 for UK-Cont.

West Africa continued to soak up some of the surplus Suezmax tonnage in the Mediterranean but most were booked for voyage back to Med/UKC. Rates for general UK/Cont options slipped to around W92.50 while more specific voyages to Italy took a more stable W100.
West Africa, transatlantic trade stayed thin but a Suezmax vessel was booked for mid-November voyage to the U.S. Gulf at a steady W92.5.
Inter UK/Cont activity was thinner today with Aframax tonnage getting the bulk of the work. Rates for 80,0000 tonne cargoes valued softer at around W107.5.
Cross Med activity continued to give Aframax tonnage reasonable employment and rates here improved slightly with Banias to Spain taking W105 and Banias/Italy achieving W107.5.
Surplus tonnage and thin demand capped rates for Suezmax tonnage at around W85 with ex-Black Sea business slow.
In the Western hemisphere moderate Caribs upcoast trade pegged rates for 70,000 tonne cargoes steady at around W130.
